headline: U.S. stock markets were closed on Thursday, November 26, 2026, in observance of Thanksgiving Day.
summary: U.S. stock markets were closed on Thursday, November 26, 2026, in observance of Thanksgiving Day. There was no regular trading session on the New York Stock Exchange or Nasdaq, and therefore no official closing prices for the major equity indexes.
overall_tone: Quiet holiday. No equity market activity occurred on November 26. Attention shifts to the abbreviated Black Friday session and the broader post-holiday trading environment.

headline: On Wednesday, November 25, 2026, U.S. stocks closed mixed after a volatile session.
summary: On Wednesday, November 25, 2026, U.S. stocks closed mixed after a volatile session. The market suffered a sharp early sell-off driven by renewed pressure on AI and technology shares, tariff concerns, and hotter inflation data, but recovered most of those losses by the close. The Dow finished higher while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended modestly lower.

us_equities.breadth: Outside of tech, breadth improved later in the day.

bonds.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield edged lower, finishing near 4.87%.

commodities.summary: Trading was relatively subdued ahead of the holiday.

currencies.summary: The VIX rose, reflecting the elevated intraday volatility (it briefly exceeded 30 in the morning before easing).

global_markets.summary: Asian markets came under pressure, with notable weakness in South Korean and Japanese tech-related shares.

key_drivers.title: Continued AI/tech weakness
key_drivers.text: Semiconductor and AI-linked stocks extended their recent pullback after Monday’s relief rally. Nvidia and other chipmakers led the early declines before partially recovering.

key_drivers.title: Inflation data
key_drivers.text: October core PCE inflation came in slightly hotter than expected (3.3% year-over-year), reinforcing expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes.

key_drivers.title: Tariff concerns
key_drivers.text: Reports of potential new U.S. tariff measures added to risk-off sentiment early in the session.

key_drivers.title: Sharp recovery
key_drivers.text: Dip-buying emerged in the afternoon, allowing the Dow to close higher and limiting losses in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Several non-tech sectors and financial names provided support.

key_drivers.title: Holiday backdrop
key_drivers.text: Trading occurred ahead of Thanksgiving (markets closed Thursday, November 26, with an early close on Friday, November 27). Volume patterns reflected the shortened week.

overall_tone: Volatile and mixed. A steep early sell-off in AI and technology stocks was largely reversed by afternoon bargain hunting, resulting in a modestly lower close for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq while the Dow finished higher. Sentiment remained fragile amid inflation data, tariff headlines, and ongoing questions about the AI trade heading into the holiday period.

headline: On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, U.S. stocks finished mixed.
summary: On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, U.S. stocks finished mixed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose and closed back above 50,000, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined as technology and semiconductor shares gave back part of the previous day’s sharp gains.

us_equities.breadth: Outside of tech, breadth was more constructive, with healthcare, some retailers, and value-oriented names performing better.

commodities.summary: Gold declined. Oil prices rose modestly.

currencies.summary: Volatility remained elevated relative to longer-term averages following the recent sharp swings.

global_markets.summary: Trading remained cautious heading into the Thanksgiving holiday period and key U.S. economic data.

key_drivers.title: Tech and AI pullback
key_drivers.text: Semiconductor and AI-linked stocks retreated after Monday’s powerful rally that was triggered by Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO. Profit-taking and lingering concerns about valuation and governance weighed on the group.

key_drivers.title: Sector rotation
key_drivers.text: Investors shifted toward value, healthcare, and select consumer names. Retailers that reported stronger results, including some that beat expectations, attracted buying.

key_drivers.title: Consumer confidence
key_drivers.text: The Conference Board’s consumer confidence index rose to its highest level in nearly two years, supported by labor-market and post-midterm optimism.

key_drivers.title: Anthropic
key_drivers.text: Shares of the newly public AI company slipped below their IPO price.

key_drivers.title: Holiday and data backdrop
key_drivers.text: Markets prepared for Wednesday’s PCE inflation data and a shortened week (closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, early close Friday).

overall_tone: Mixed and rotational. The Dow advanced and reclaimed the 50,000 level on broader participation outside technology, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq retreated as AI and chip stocks cooled after Monday’s surge. Sentiment remained sensitive to leadership news, valuation concerns, and the upcoming holiday-shortened trading schedule.

headline: On Monday, November 23, 2026, U.S. stocks staged a powerful relief rally, snapping a seven-day losing streak and lifting the S&P 500 and Dow out of correction territory.
summary: On Monday, November 23, 2026, U.S. stocks staged a powerful relief rally, snapping a seven-day losing streak and lifting the S&P 500 and Dow out of correction territory. Technology and AI-related shares led the advance after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

us_equities.breadth: Market breadth was robust, with advancing stocks far outnumbering decliners.

bonds.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield edged slightly higher, finishing near 4.92%.

commodities.summary: Oil prices declined. Gold was mixed to higher in some reports.
commodities.gold: Gold was mixed to higher in some reports.

currencies.summary: Volatility eased significantly, with the VIX falling more than 25% to around 26.6.

global_markets.summary: The rebound in U.S. tech and AI sentiment provided a positive tone heading into the shortened holiday week.

key_drivers.title: Nvidia leadership news
key_drivers.text: The board’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO triggered a massive relief rally in Nvidia shares and the broader AI/semiconductor complex, reversing much of the prior week’s heavy selling.

key_drivers.title: Recovery from correction
key_drivers.text: The S&P 500 and Dow recovered enough ground to exit formal correction territory (the >10% decline from recent highs). The S&P 500 regained more than half of the previous week’s losses.

key_drivers.title: AI and tech leadership
key_drivers.text: Semiconductors and AI-related stocks dominated the upside, with strong participation from names tied to data centers and infrastructure. Defensive sectors lagged relatively.

key_drivers.title: Volatility decline
key_drivers.text: The sharp drop in the VIX reflected a rapid shift in sentiment after the intense selling of the prior week.

key_drivers.title: Holiday context
key_drivers.text: Trading occurred ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday (markets closed Thursday, November 26, with an early close on Friday, November 27).

overall_tone: Strongly positive and risk-on. A dramatic rebound driven by the Nvidia leadership reversal allowed major indexes to snap a multi-day losing streak, exit correction territory, and post some of their largest single-day gains in over a year. Technology and AI stocks led the charge as investors returned following the prior week’s severe sell-off.

headline: On Friday, November 20, 2026, U.S. stocks plunged in a sharp AI-driven sell-off.
summary: On Friday, November 20, 2026, U.S. stocks plunged in a sharp AI-driven sell-off. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both entered correction territory (more than 10% below their recent highs), the Nasdaq suffered one of its largest one-day point drops on record and turned negative for the year, and the S&P 500 extended its losing streak to seven consecutive sessions—its longest since February 2020.

us_equities.breadth: Breadth was extremely weak, with the vast majority of stocks falling.

bonds.summary: Treasury yields edged lower as investors sought safer assets amid the equity rout. The 10-year yield moved lower during the session.

commodities.summary: Gold fell sharply (down roughly 4%). Crude oil rose modestly.

currencies.summary: The dollar remained relatively firm. Volatility surged, with the VIX climbing more than 26% to around 35.9—its highest close in several months.

global_markets.summary: Risk-off sentiment was evident internationally, with Asian markets under pressure in subsequent trading.

key_drivers.title: Intensifying AI trade unwind
key_drivers.text: Selling in AI and semiconductor stocks accelerated. Nvidia led the declines amid reports of regulatory scrutiny, while other chipmakers and AI-related names also dropped sharply. Anthropic’s post-IPO performance failed to stabilize sentiment.

key_drivers.title: Correction confirmed
key_drivers.text: Both the S&P 500 and the Dow closed more than 10% below their recent record highs, formally entering correction territory. The Nasdaq’s heavy losses pushed it into negative territory for the year.

key_drivers.title: Weekly performance
key_drivers.text: The major indexes posted their worst weekly percentage declines since April 2025 (or earlier for the Nasdaq). The S&P 500’s seven-day losing streak was its longest since early 2020.

key_drivers.title: Defensive rotation
key_drivers.text: Investors rotated toward more defensive areas such as consumer staples, while growth and technology sectors absorbed the heaviest selling.

key_drivers.title: Volatility spike
key_drivers.text: The sharp rise in the VIX reflected heightened fear and forced selling in some areas.

overall_tone: Deeply risk-off and negative. A broad and aggressive unwind of the AI trade drove major indexes into correction territory, erased most or all of the year’s gains for key benchmarks, and produced the worst weekly performance in more than a year. Volatility rose sharply as the multi-day sell-off intensified into the weekend.
